I am a quantitative researcher who studies support for housing and housing policies in Canada. I currently work at the [Global Migration Institute](https://www.torontomu.ca/global-migration-institute/) at Toronto Metropolitan University, where I study [housing for international students](https://www.torontomu.ca/bridging-divides/research/research-projects/place-and-infrastructure/housing-for-international-students/) as part Bridging Divides' Place and Infrastructure theme. I also examine individual level support for housing as part of a project with the Laurier Institute for the Study of Public Opinion and Policy ([LISPOP](https://scholars.wlu.ca/lispop/4/)) which has been featured in the [Waterloo Region Record](https://www.therecord.com/opinion/contributors/waterloo-s-housing-crisis-puts-densification-to-the-test/article_ec96d782-3b1c-58e7-a993-faf8aa6b744a.html).

Additionally, I have been mapping results of the [2026 Montréal election](montreal_election.qmd), examining [Bixi Rides](bixi-world-cup.qmd) during the world cup, and maintain [Thoughts at the End of the Mile](https://rafaelcg01.substack.com/) a Substack about Montreal politics, planning, and history. I have previously contributed to the Canadian Election Study ([CES](http://www.ces-eec.ca)) and worked extensively as a research assistant for the Laurier Institute for the Study of Public Opinion and Policy ([LISPOP](https://lispop.ca)), Université du Québec à Montréal, and the Centre for the Study of Democratic Citizenship.

I received a Master's Degree in Political Science from [McGill University](https://www.mcgill.ca/politicalscience/) and a Bachelor's degree in Political Science from [Wilfrid Laurier University](https://students.wlu.ca/programs/arts/political-science/index.html).
